reading.body:
Clay White is named on five Lobbying Disclosure Act filings about AI, all filed through one lobbying firm for a single client, the AI Policy Network.

The pattern is narrow and concentrated. Five filings, one firm, one client, and eighteen bills named across them. The disclosed prior government positions are staff roles for two Utah congressmen, Chris Stewart and Jason Chaffetz, which the Lobbying Disclosure Act requires filers to list for the prior twenty years. That is the standard disclosure, not an unusual one.

For AI specifically, this is the legislative layer of the buildout. Bills get numbered, lobbyists get retained, and the compute, buildings, and power that the site tracks elsewhere are downstream of rules that are still being written. The data shows who is registered to influence that writing. It does not show what they argued, what the bills would do, or whether any passed.

What the record does not cover matters as much as what it does. It gives no dollar amounts, no committee assignments, no meetings, and no outcomes. It also flags that a different lobbyist shares the name, so the five filings here should not be merged with any other Clay White.
